question: Should OpenClaw core own a first-party per-agent restore/clone command, and if so what exact state, credential, transcript, and rename semantics are allowed?
rationale: The requested workflow crosses destructive local state writes, config rewriting, credential portability, private session history, and overlapping backup/migration work, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Define Minimal Core Per-Agent Restore
options.body: Sponsor a preview-first `backup create --agent` and restore/clone contract with explicit include/exclude rules, path validation, rollback, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Backup Restore Design
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until the broader native backup/restore umbrella chooses a shared archive format and restore safety model.

options.title: Route Clone Workflow Outside Core
options.body: Leave core focused on archive verification and missing APIs while a plugin or ClawHub package owns optional per-agent clone workflows that do not need privileged state rewrites.

recommendation.title: Define Minimal Core Per-Agent Restore
recommendation.body: Sponsor a preview-first `backup create --agent` and restore/clone contract with explicit include/exclude rules, path validation, rollback, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is a product/security boundary decision across core backup, restore, sessions, and ClawHub/plugin scope, and prior review context points to this routing role.
